content: SHREVEPORT, La. ( KTAL/KMSS ) — Fall is quickly approaching, which means respiratory virus season is right around the corner. Doctors say infants are the most susceptible to respiratory viruses. RSV, or Respiratory Syncytial Virus, is the most common virus that puts newborns at risk for pneumonia and airway inflammation. Shreveport doctor urges UV safety during heat rise Experts say the easiest way for parents to protect their little ones is to keep their environment as germ-free as possible. With recent advancements in medicine, physicians say it is best to talk with your child's medical provider to see if vaccinations are best for them. "So, for the first time, families have access to multiple ways to actually build a shield around their newborn before the RSV actually reaches that baby," says Dr. David Janese, family medicine physician with Ochsner LSU Health. PCOS now PMOS: New name reflects broader health impact "So make sure that you stay informed, you're asking questions, you're doing your own research, because when it comes down to it, you're the parent. You're the protector of your child. You have to do what you want to do, and we want to do what's best for the baby," Janese says. Dr. Janese says if your baby has a fever, trouble breathing, and is less responsive, contact your child's pediatrician. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved.
